title: Contract Pricing Agreement Notice Relief on Early-Termination Rebate Forfeiture
content:
# Extra termination notice and rebate forfeiture relief — Contract Pricing Agreement

**Rule.** When a Contract Pricing Agreement is terminated early, the notice relief follows the extra notice, which is the calendar days from the date the customer's written termination notice was received to the termination effective date, less the tier's early termination notice period. The relief is subtracted from the termination period's net rebate before the forfeiture's floor at 0.00 and its rounding to the cent are applied.

| Extra notice | Notice relief |
|---|---|
| 90 or more extra days | 0.05 times the termination period's net rebate |
| At least 1 and fewer than 90 extra days | 0.025 times the termination period's net rebate |
| Fewer than one extra day | No notice relief |

**Tier notice periods (calendar days).**

| Tier | Early termination notice |
|---|---|
| Corbett Account Price Schedule | 30 |
| Corbett Volume Discount Agreement | 30 |
| Corbett Category Contract | 60 |
| Corbett Net-Price Contract | 90 |
| Corbett Cost-Plus Contract | 90 |
| Corbett Strategic Supply Agreement | 180 |

Calendar days from one date to another count the later date and not the earlier one. Wherever a latest record of a kind is taken, it is the one with the latest date, and among records of the same date the one recorded first.

**Example (hypothetical dates and figures).** On a tier with a 90 day notice period, a notice received 200 calendar days before the termination effective date gives 200 less 90, which is 110 extra days; on a net rebate of 1000.00 the relief is 50.00. A notice received exactly 90 days before gives 0 extra days and no relief.
